sections.heading: Overview
sections.content:
The Cable Loaded Row Machine is a seated rowing exercise performed on a plate-loaded or cable-loaded machine with a fixed movement path.

This exercise primarily targets the muscles of the mid and upper back, including the latissimus dorsi, rhomboids, and trapezius.

The machine provides a stable, guided range of motion, making it an excellent option for isolating back muscles while minimizing lower back strain.

sections.heading: Benefits
sections.content:
- Targets the mid and upper back effectively
- Guided movement path reduces risk of injury
- Minimal lower back stress compared to free-weight rows
- Easy to adjust resistance for progressive overload
- Encourages proper scapular retraction
- Great for building back thickness and width
- Suitable for all fitness levels from beginner to advanced

sections.heading: Muscles Worked
sections.content:
Primary: Latissimus Dorsi, Rhomboids, Trapezius (Mid/Lower)

Secondary: Rear Deltoids, Biceps, Forearms, Erector Spinae, Core

sections.heading: Starting Position
sections.content:
1. Sit on the machine with your feet flat on the footrests.
2. Adjust the chest pad or seat height so the handles are at mid-chest level.
3. Grasp the handles with an overhand grip, arms fully extended.
4. Sit with your back straight, chest up, and shoulders down and back.
5. Engage your core to maintain a stable torso throughout the movement.

sections.heading: Execution
sections.content:
1. Keep your arms extended in front of you to start.
2. Pull the handles towards your torso by driving your elbows back.
3. Focus on squeezing your shoulder blades together at the peak of the movement.
4. Pause briefly at the fully contracted position.
5. Slowly release the handles back to the starting position with control.
6. Maintain a straight back and avoid using momentum.
7. Repeat the movement for the desired number of reps.

sections.heading: Common Mistakes
sections.content:
- Using momentum or jerking the weight instead of controlled pulling
- Rounding the back during the movement
- Shrugging shoulders up towards ears
- Not fully retracting the shoulder blades at peak contraction
- Pulling with the arms instead of initiating with the back
- Leaning too far back during the pull
- Using too heavy a weight, compromising form
- Rushing through reps without pausing at the contraction point

sections.heading: Equipment Needed
sections.content:
- Cable Loaded Row Machine
- Weight Plates (for plate-loaded versions)
- Optional: Lifting Gloves or Straps (for grip assistance)
- Optional: Chalk (improves grip on handles)

sections.heading: Machine Setup
sections.content:
1. Adjust the seat height so the handles align with your mid-chest.
2. Set the chest pad (if available) to allow full arm extension.
3. Select an appropriate weight for your fitness level.
4. Ensure the foot plates are positioned so your knees are slightly bent.
5. Check that the cable or pulley system moves smoothly before starting.

sections.heading: Body Setup
sections.content:
1. Feet: Flat and firmly planted on the footrests.
2. Knees: Slightly bent for stability.
3. Torso: Upright with a neutral spine.
4. Chest: Pressed lightly against the pad (if applicable).
5. Shoulders: Down and back, away from ears.
6. Grip: Overhand, shoulder-width apart on the handles.
7. Core: Engaged throughout the exercise.
8. Head: Neutral, looking straight ahead.

sections.heading: Similar Exercises
sections.content:
- Seated Cable Row: Free cable version with more stabilization required
- Barbell Bent Over Row: Free-weight compound row movement
- Single Arm Dumbbell Row: Unilateral back work for muscle balance
- T-Bar Row: Barbell variation with chest support option
- Lat Pulldown: Vertical pulling for lat development
- Inverted Row: Bodyweight alternative for back training

sections.heading: Machine Row Variations
sections.content:
Cable Loaded Row Machine: Standard seated row with guided path
Wide Grip Row: Wider hand position for upper back emphasis
Close Grip Row: Narrow grip for lat and mid-back focus
Underhand Grip Row: Supinated grip for more bicep engagement
Single Arm Machine Row: Unilateral version for imbalance correction
Pause Rep Row: Added pause at contraction for increased time under tension

sections.heading: If You Have Limitations
sections.content:
Shoulder Issues: Use a neutral grip and reduce range of motion
Lower Back Pain: Ensure chest pad support, keep torso upright
Wrist Discomfort: Try neutral or underhand grip variations
Grip Fatigue: Use lifting straps for heavier sets
No Machine Available: Substitute with seated cable rows or resistance band rows
Learning Stage: Start with light weight, focus on the mind-muscle connection with the back
